4_1_full_proof_architecture: Insert the particular displayed fixed alternating tangle into each graph vertex of D1, obtaining a reduced alternating link diagram D1bar.
Use the ordinary reduced-alternating minimal-crossing result cited as [10] to know D1bar is minimal for its underlying link.
Transport the identical local insertions through the isometrically prepared given f, obtaining an equivalent-link diagram D2bar. The source EXPLICITLY does not assume D2bar is alternating.
Minimality yields c(D2bar)>=c(D1bar). Because inserted tangles correspond isometrically, c(D2)-c(D1)=c(D2bar)-c(D1bar), so c(D2)>=c(D1).
Apply the same argument to f inverse, giving the reverse inequality. Thus every triple has c(D1)=c(D2).
what_4_1_resolves: The two diagrams of a triple have a common crossing count, giving the announced induction a well-defined common size. It also supplies the graph crossing-number context used in the previously read4.8nullification argument, although its exact application there remains an actual diagrammatic step, not replaced by this report.
